author: Codex difficulty pair A

source_artifacts.claim: Authored level_03 defines the ferry, stop and rescue pads, hero-specific gates, slime, and exits.
Hold/latch effects control the motor and barriers.
Moving ferry carries riders when powered and not braked.
Ferry labels expose NO POWER, moving, and STOP states.

prior_knowledge.concept: Isp hold and Pac persistent rescue latch

evidence.claim: First room introduced Isp hold followed by Pac rescue latch.

prior_knowledge.concept: Moving carrier with repeated boarding opportunity

evidence.claim: The preceding lift room introduced moving carrier boarding and repeated motion.

prior_knowledge.concept: Slime gap crossing and full-room retry after a fall

evidence.claim: The preceding bridge room introduced a slime gap and a lethal fall risk.

prior_knowledge.concept: Isp brakes a horizontal motorized ferry while Pac boards and reaches rescue

evidence.claim: Current ferry, STOP motor effect, and Pac RESCUE create a new brake-and-carry relationship.

mechanics.fact: Isp's STOP temporarily brakes the horizontal ferry and opens only Pac's landing gate.

evidence.claim: The STOP hold effect targets ferry motor and pac_landing door.
Active motor effect turns motor off.

mechanics.fact: Pac's RESCUE [L] permanently opens both the Pac landing and Isp rescue membranes after occupation.

evidence.claim: Pac latch targets both barriers.
Latch persists and opens doors.

mechanics.fact: The blue Pac-landing membrane at x725 blocks Pac only; the orange Isp-rescue membrane at x900 blocks Isp only. An open membrane can remain outlined on screen.

evidence.claim: Barrier owner and positions are explicit.
Diagnostic explains the hero-specific barriers and visible open outline.

mechanics.fact: The ferry cycles horizontally and carries riders when the brake is released. Gem's bubble can briefly FLOAT Isp off STOP, interrupting the brake, then Isp can return.

evidence.claim: Bubble and ferry motion are authored.
Ferry displacement carries riders.
FLOAT is time-limited.

mechanics.fact: Missing a ferry-to-bank jump can drop a hero into slime, causing an automatic fresh-room retry.

evidence.claim: Left shore, ferry, and right shore surround the gap.
Slime harms both heroes.
Death increments retry and resets the state.

legal_routes.name: Ordinary-key brake, Pac rescue, Isp follow, both exits

steps.goal: Position the ferry and open Pac's landing
steps.action: Move Isp to STOP and hold while Pac boards or approaches the ferry.
steps.expected_feedback: The ferry shows STOP and Pac's landing gate opens.

evidence.claim: Isp STOP brakes ferry and opens Pac landing.
Accepted route first moves Isp right toward STOP.

steps.goal: Cross the gap and latch rescue
steps.action: Move Pac onto the ferry; use the brake and cyclic ferry position to transfer to the right shore, then occupy RESCUE.
steps.expected_feedback: The latch opens both far-bank membranes.
steps.observed_feedback: The accepted completion state displays + PAC RESCUE [L].

evidence.claim: Ferry and Pac rescue are defined.
Accepted route moves Pac toward the ferry.
Completed room displays active Pac RESCUE latch.

steps.action: Once RESCUE is latched, move Isp onto the ferry, ride/jump to the right shore, and continue through the open Isp membrane.
steps.expected_feedback: Both gates remain open even after Pac leaves RESCUE.
steps.observed_feedback: A native continuation of the separate first-use inputs moves Isp through both open membranes and completes; the built-browser route also clears.

evidence.claim: Pac latch opens both barriers persistently.
Native ordinary-D continuation passes both gates after an idle apparent block.
Accepted campaign route uses Isp jump/right after Pac's crossing.

steps.action: Continue right until Isp and Pac overlap their matching exits.
steps.observed_feedback: The accepted built-browser result is complete with zero retries.

evidence.claim: Matching exits are on right shore.
Fourth campaign position completes.
Authored ferry and gate route.
Ordinary built-browser clear.
Independent native continuation resolves the apparent gate block.

isp: Holds STOP to brake the ferry and open Pac's landing.
After Pac latches RESCUE, boards and crosses to Isp exit.
pac: Boards/crosses while Isp controls the ferry and landing gate.
Latches RESCUE to keep both membranes open for Isp, then reaches Pac exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Jump toward the far shore before the ferry or landing is aligned.
common_mistakes.consequence: A hero may fall into slime and trigger an automatic full-room retry; the separate first-use AI attempt actually lost Isp this way.
common_mistakes.recovery: After reset, time Pac's boarding while Isp brakes, then use the ferry and latch RESCUE before Isp follows.

evidence.claim: Ferry lies between two shores.
Slime is lethal.
Death auto-resets.
First-use room-four attempt witnessed an Isp fall and retry.

common_mistakes.mistake: Gem's bubble lifts Isp off STOP during Pac's ferry ride.
common_mistakes.consequence: The brake releases and the ferry resumes motion while Isp is away from the pad; this can change Pac's boarding position.
common_mistakes.recovery: Wait for FLOAT to expire and move Isp back onto STOP, or continue after Pac reaches the persistent RESCUE latch.

evidence.claim: Gem bubble targets the stop area.
STOP is temporary while RESCUE latches.
FLOAT expires after a short duration.
Separate first-use AI observed a temporary float and return to brake.

common_mistakes.mistake: Interpret Isp standing near a visible blue membrane as a closed-gate deadlock.
common_mistakes.consequence: The separate source-blind AI observer stopped after an idle input and inferred a closed gate; native replay shows RESCUE latched, both gates open, and Isp safely on the right bank.
common_mistakes.recovery: Continue holding D. The native replay moves Isp through the open membranes and reaches both exits.

evidence.claim: Original source-blind interpretation remains a recorded observation, not a source fact.
The final action had no keys and ordinary D continuation cleared.
RESCUE latch opens both membranes.

optional_collectibles: Two owner-specific sparks sit over the ferry and near the far exit. The accepted route collected 2/2, but neither spark is needed by the both-exit condition.

reasoning.rationale: Isp must brake and open Pac's landing, Pac must board/cross and latch rescue, then Isp follows. The plan combines familiar latch logic with ferry control.

evidence.claim: STOP and RESCUE jointly control motor and gates.

cooperation.rationale: The ferry/landing handoff requires Isp's temporary support and Pac's persistent rescue; both then cross to their own exits.

evidence.claim: Pads accept opposite heroes and support each other's crossing.

execution.rationale: Boarding, riding, and leaving a horizontal ferry over slime require several controlled transfers. The first-use AI fell short once, although the accepted route clears.

evidence.claim: Moving ferry separates two shores.
Separate first-use AI witnessed a failed far-bank transfer.
Accepted route demonstrates a clean clear.

timing.rationale: The ferry cycles and STOP can arrest it; Gem can briefly release the brake. These are readable, repeatable windows with pauses available on shore.

evidence.claim: Bubble attack and cyclic ferry motion.
STOP is temporary and RESCUE persistent.

hazards.rationale: The mandatory ferry crossing spans lethal slime, with a witnessed fall on a separate first-use AI attempt.

evidence.claim: Shore-ferry-shore geometry.
Slime harms both heroes.
First-use AI actually fell and retried.

novelty.rationale: The new causal element is braking a motorized horizontal carrier; earlier rooms introduced moving carriers, hold/latch pads, and slime crossings separately.

evidence.claim: STOP adds motor control to the familiar handoff.
Earlier vertical lift introduced moving platform travel.

recovery_cost.rationale: A slime fall resets a multi-stage ferry and latch sequence; a safe bubble interruption only requires waiting and retaking STOP.

evidence.claim: Lethal fall triggers fresh-room retry.
Separate first-use AI lost a crossing and restarted.
FLOAT is temporary.

solution_clarity.rationale: STOP/RESCUE labels cue the core handoff, but a membrane remains visibly outlined when open; a separate AI observer misread an idle position as a gate block. This is a cue ambiguity hypothesis, not a measured human failure.

evidence.claim: Core pad and barrier relations.
Renderer draws membranes in either state.
Diagnostic distinguishes open outline, idle input, and successful continuation.

control_friction.rationale: The accepted ordinary-key browser journey and native D continuation show working control response. The apparent gate block followed no rightward input, not a failed key.

evidence.claim: Built-browser zero-retry clear.
Native reproduction identifies idle input and successful D continuation.

confidence_reason: Authored mechanics, accepted built-browser clear, first-use failed attempt, and native continuation establish route and error causes. Human interpretation remains unmeasured.

confirmed: The frozen first pass correctly proposed Isp STOP, Pac ferry crossing to RESCUE, Isp follow, and both exits.
The moving ferry and slime gap do create timing, movement, and hazard demands; sparks are optional.
missed_mechanics: STOP opens Pac's landing only while Isp occupies it; RESCUE latches both membranes open for Isp to follow.
The blue landing membrane blocks Pac only, not Isp; the orange rescue membrane blocks Isp only.
A visible membrane outline can remain when the gate is open.
Gem's temporary FLOAT can release STOP, after which Isp can reoccupy it.
incorrect_inferences: The paired first pass did not assert a closed-gate deadlock. Separately, the source-blind first-use AI observer inferred one from a final idle frame; native replay shows that final action released all keys and ordinary D input crosses both open gates.
changed_judgments: Execution 2 -> 3: source and first-use fall show multiple controlled ferry transfers over slime.
Recovery cost null -> 3: a fall restarts the multi-step brake, ferry, and latch sequence, while a bubble interruption has local recovery.
Control friction null -> 0: built-browser and native ordinary-key continuations demonstrate responsive controls; the source-blind stillness was an idle input.
unresolved: Whether two uncoached humans would also misread the open membrane outline is unknown.
Human difficulty, enjoyment, and key-sharing comfort remain unmeasured.

single_operator_note: One operator must hold Isp's STOP while steering Pac through a moving ferry crossing, then switch to Isp's keys after Pac latches RESCUE. This adds coordination beyond the two-human baseline.
